label: Source search for bare and supported premises under the Fourth Way grades step, the uniter bridges…
summary: Source search for bare and supported premises under the Fourth Way grades step (#982), the uniter bridges (#983) and the esse-reception bridges (#976). Searched the Latin of Summa contra gentiles I-III on Corpus Thomisticum (sentence-level search of all chapters, 2026-11-05) and the already pinned Posterior Analytics I.2 and De potentia q.3 a.5. STATED: (1) STMT-EXCEEDED-PERFECTION-IS-CAUSED by SCG II.15 n.3 [24524] 'Quod igitur alicui minus convenit quam aliis, non convenit ei ex sua natura tantum, sed ex alia causa' (claim AQUINAS-SCG-II-15-LESSER-HAS-IT-FROM-ANOTHER-CAUSE; interpretive step: 'alia causa' as a cause other than the bearer). De potentia q.3 a.5 co., secunda ratio, was set aside as the stating text: it says what has a diversely participated perfection imperfectly receives it from that in which it is most perfect, which presupposes a most perfect bearer, and its warrant 'si unicuique eorum ex se ipso illud conveniret' is a not-every, not a for-every. (2) SCG I.18 n.4 [23649] 'Componens autem est causa efficiens compositi' states the time-neutral STMT-COMPOSER-IS-EFFICIENT-CAUSE-OF-COMPOSITE (claim AQUINAS-SCG-I-18-COMPOSER-IS-EFFICIENT-CAUSE). A first version bound it to STMT-UNITING-CAUSE-IS-EFFICIENT; Codex review on #995 rightly rejected that, because EfficientlyCausesIn is here-and-now efficient causing and the sentence does not say that a past composer is a present cause. It is now a supports relation. (3) STMT-CAUSE-OF-QUALITY-IN-ANOTHER-IS-MORE-SUCH by Posterior Analytics I.2, 72a29-30 'ἀεὶ γὰρ δι᾿ ὃ ὑπάρχει ἕκαστον, ἐκεῖνο μᾶλλον ὑπάρχει' (claim ARIST-APOST-72A-CAUSE-MORE-SUCH), which carries no synonymy condition; SCG 'causa potior est effectu' (I.41 n.4, III.77 n.6, III.120 n.18) and 'causa est nobilior effectu' (I.18 n.5) compare cause and effect simply, not per quality, and were not used. SUPPORTED: STMT-UNITING-CAUSE-IS-EFFICIENT (temporal gap) and STMT-UNITING-CAUSE-CAUSES-COMPOSITE-BEING by SCG I.18 n.4 (efficient cause of the composite; esse is not named). No SCG I-III sentence says the composer or uniter gives the composite its esse. NOT FOUND: STMT-NO-INFINITE-REGRESS-OF-CAUSES-OF-A-PERFECTION. SCG I.15 n.5 and II.15 n.6 deny infinite regress for two perfection-indexed series only (causes of being of what can be and not be; causes of necessity), I.13 n.33 and II.38 n.13 for efficient causes, I.38 n.4 for final causes. Counter-evidence to the cycle-excluding reading: SCG III.14 n.2 [25664] says that infinite regress in causes is avoided 'propter circulum inventum in causis et causatis secundum species diversas causarum' (matter and form, agent and end cause each other in different respects). Those circles are not indexed to one perfection, so they do not falsify the premise, but a mixed-species well-foundedness claim needs a text that indexes by the perfection caused, and none was found. NOT FOUND: STMT-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN-OWN-ESSENCE. SCG I.43 n.5 ('omnis actus alteri inhaerens terminationem recipit ex eo in quo est'; God's esse 'nec ... inhaeret alicui formae vel naturae') and I.69 n.7 ('esse receptum et limitatum ad aliquam speciem vel genus') speak of esse received in a form, nature or species, not of the thing's own essence for every x. Counter-evidence: SCG II.80 n.13 says of the human soul united to the body that 'subiectum ipsum recipiens est corpus'. This is now recorded as an attack (REL-UNITED-SOUL-ESSE-RECEIVED-BY-BODY-ATTACKS-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN-OWN-ESSENCE), with its reading choices. NOT FOUND: STMT-NOTHING-IN-RECEPTIVE-POTENCY-TO-ITSELF. 'quod est in altero, est in eo per modum recipientis' (I.43 n.5), 'Omne quod est in aliquo est in eo per modum recipientis' (II.50 n.6), 'Receptum est in recipiente per modum recipientis' (II.73 n.31, II.74 n.8) and 'Nihil recipit quod iam habet' (II.73 n.30) do not state irreflexivity; I.23 n.3 ('idem secundum idem faceret seipsum in actu') concerns causing what one receives, not receiving oneself. Not yet searched: SCG IV, De veritate, Quodlibeta, In De causis, Liber de causis, and secondary literature.
blocker: No pinned text states the regress premise, the uniter-causes-esse bridge or either esse-reception bridge. Stating claims leave route cost unchanged: a stated premise remains one open leaf under corpus.py root_routes.
